prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which established the basis of incretin-based therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single B004 part for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with a citation confined to the discovery domain. The scientific case has not weakened after the full exchange. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and glucose-dependent insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor actions, and Mojsov identified and synthesised the biologically active truncated peptide that made the physiology tractable. The resulting drugs have been validated in large, independent randomised trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism is understood and replicated over decades, so there is no maturity question. All six of us now converge on B004, and I note that the chair's summary shows the arguments rest on the science, not on the opening count. I would reach the same view if the count were five other candidates.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution, not merit. Habener's proglucagon and GLP-1 work is outside the credited names, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to his group cannot be settled from the supplied record. I also accept that omitting Knudsen leaves the drugs people actually take uncredited, so the prize could read as honouring the idea but not the delivery. A three-person cap means every B004 configuration is partial. A citation that names the active form of the peptide risks implying a priority judgement that we cannot verify, so the wording should be kept general enough not to adjudicate between Mojsov and Habener.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Knudsen as third laureate with a citation spanning physiology and drug development, while saying he could accept Mojsov if the committee confines the citation to discovery.
responses.response: I take your Knudsen argument seriously, and I agree the incretin hormone would not have become a drug without durable acylated agonists. Where I differ is on what a Nobel Prize for discovery should anchor. A span to drug development would add an industrial programme while the prize still left out the peptide identification, and under a three-person cap it forces out either Holst, Drucker or Mojsov, each of whom has a discovery contribution that stands independently. You said you could accept Mojsov if the citation is confined to discovery. I think that is the right framing, and with five of six of us already there, I would ask you to weigh the discovery-first trio on its own merits and not as a concession.

responses.point: Perlmann says the Knudsen question is the main disagreement on B004 and deserves a deliberate vote, and prefers B032 as a clean-attribution case that could crowd out less well-attributed candidates.
responses.response: I agree the Knudsen question should be settled by a deliberate vote, and I have changed my own position on it from opening to now. I also share your view that B032 has the cleanest attribution on the list, with Mori and Walter as an obvious pair. That is why I move it into my alternatives. My hesitation is the one Sandberg raised: B032 beside B004 would exceed the three-person cap, so it can only replace part of the GLP-1 trio. I do not think a very clean story for a mechanism with developing clinical consequences should displace a discovery chain with proven outcomes. It is a strong candidate for a year when that comparison does not arise.

responses.point: Svenningsson says the committee should test Mojsov's priority claim against the documentary record before the final ballot, and carry the Habener uncertainty into the citation wording.
responses.response: I agree with both parts. On the record, the supplied material does not allow me to rank Mojsov's identification of the active peptide against the early proglucagon work from Habener's group, and I do not think we should settle it by preference. I would not alter the laureates on that uncertainty alone, because Mojsov's contribution on the active truncated peptide is a distinct and necessary step. I do accept your suggestion that the wording should carry the uncertainty. My revised citation therefore speaks of the biologically active form of GLP-1 in general terms and does not claim first identification. If the documentary record before the ballot clearly favoured another credit, I would reconsider the third name.

responses.point: Sandberg observes that a second part such as B032 would give five people and exceed the cap, so it competes with a three-person GLP-1 prize and does not add to it, and he sees B043 as a risky second part because of six credited names.
responses.response: I agree with your arithmetic. A two-part prize would force B004 to two names, and the two I would keep, Holst and Drucker, would leave out the identification of the active peptide that I regard as decisive. I also agree that B043 has the worst attribution problem, which is why I have dropped it from my alternatives and replaced it with B032, whose credit is unambiguous. For B018 I keep it as an alternative but only in the narrower June and Sadelain form, as you noted yourself that Eshhar's absence is not repaired by adding Rosenberg. I therefore see a single-part prize as the better use of the three places this year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would accept Knudsen only if the committee decides the citation should explicitly honour drug development, and calls a B004 plus B032 pairing a defensible fallback.
responses.response: I agree that the citation should decide the third name, not the reverse, and that is why I am keeping it on discovery. I take your B004 plus B032 pairing seriously as a fallback but I do not think it is workable under the cap, since it would leave only one GLP-1 laureate and exclude at least one of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov, none of whom I regard as dispensable. I would prefer the committee not to trade a complete chain for a second part this year. I also share your view that B018 and B043 are better held as alternatives, and my alternatives now reflect that for B018, with B032 replacing B043 on attribution grounds.

uncertainties: Whether Habener's contribution to proglucagon and GLP-1 peptide work outweighs Mojsov's, and whether the citation can avoid adjudicating it.
Whether the committee will vote for a discovery-centred citation (Mojsov) or a translational one (Knudsen), a choice I regard as a judgement and not a factual question.
Whether a CAR-T prize can be credited defensibly without Eshhar, and whether June and Sadelain alone is an adequate two-person form of B018.
Whether B032 is better treated as a standalone future candidate than as a second part, given the three-person cap.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict. My documented connections are co-authorship of the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and shared publications with colleagues, including Sandberg (who disclosed this in round 1). None of these involves a credited name on the shortlist. I have still not checked every candidate's complete publication record.
